newsitem.title: UK: LME markets softer, June pricing goes smoothly.
newsitem.headline: LME markets softer, June pricing goes smoothly.

text.p: Base metal trading remained slow during Monday's official LME sessions, with traders saying that pricing against the June date was unexciting and that it had little effect on the market.

Prices were slightly lower in most cases, largely a reflection of the copper market where prices are correcting back from last week's overbought levels above $2,600. Warehouse stock data had little impact.
"Third Wednesday was pretty much a non-event, really. At one stage it looked as if copper was not going to trade at all, and if you blinked you would have missed it," one trader said.

Stocks fell by 1,875 tonnes, which aided downside stability as there were not any deliveries into the U.S. or Singapore, although warrants for the latter location are changing hands at a very low $5, some noted.
Prices perked up towards session highs during the kerb on U.S.-based speculative covering, with last trade at $2,584 a tonne, still down $6 from last Friday's kerb close.

In aluminium, a flurry of cash pricing sales were checked by short-covering, and in subsequent kerb business the market clawed back some early losses. However, last trade was at $1,584, still down $2 from pre-weekend levels.
Another 3,850-tonne stock fall did not bolster the market significantly, as the general trend of LME metal declines could by inventory re-distribution.
Also, the heavy lending of June/July late last week has defused the tightness that was developing, with the overall cash/threes contango widening out to $27/28, against levels near $20 a week ago.
Nickel crumbled from the outset, with the market becoming increasingly passe about the current stoppage at Inco Sudbury and Norilsk's gas supply problems.
"If it cannot respond to problems at the world's two biggest producers it must be in bad shape," one trader said.
Last morning business was at $7,260, down $80 a tonne from pre-weekend levels.
The rest of the complex was featureless, with lead drifting back to $621, an $8 loss, while zinc was $2 lower at $1,372.
Tin also fell away gently, and was $15 easier at $5,565, while alloy lost $10 at $1,470.
